elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2: "Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents ... and defend and save each of them harmless" — an express defence duty running to AbbVie and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2: indemnity "from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees"; "AbbVie Indemnitees" expressly includes AbbVie's Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The enumerated bases of Section 11.2 are redacted ("arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]"). Section 7.4 makes Third Party patent-infringement claims against AbbVie "Subject to Section 11.2", which implies but does not evidence IP coverage; the operative trigger text cannot be read. Deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" returned false, consistent with the redaction rather than with confirmed absence.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2's trigger list is redacted ("[***]"); no other rendered provision addresses Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law as an indemnity basis.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2's trigger list is redacted; nothing in the rendered text addresses unauthorised access to or disclosure of AbbVie information caused by Harpoon.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2's trigger list is redacted. Section 11.5's carve-out of fraud, wilful misconduct and gross negligence from the consequential-damages exclusion is a liability-limitation carve-out, not an indemnity trigger, so it does not evidence this element.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 11.3: "The Indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice (an 'Indemnification Claim Notice') of any Losses or discovery of fact upon which such Indemnified Party intends to base a request for indemnification under this Article 11"; no forfeiture for delay absent prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4.1: "at its option, the indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim by giving written notice to the Indemnified Party within [***] after ... receipt of an Indemnification Claim Notice" — control is allocated (the redacted interval is a period, not the allocation itself).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4.4: "the Indemnified Party shall, and shall cause each indemnitee to, cooperate in the defense or prosecution thereof and shall furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1's bases for AbbVie's indemnity of the Harpoon Indemnitees are redacted ("arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]"), so the scope cannot be confirmed as confined to AbbVie-provided content and AbbVie's breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same defect as the preferred IP element: the Section 11.2 trigger list is redacted, so no operative IP-infringement trigger can be verified in the rendered text.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification-based exclusion appears in the rendered Article 11, and its absence is Customer-favourable, so the permission is satisfied without change.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination-based exclusion appears in the rendered text; absence is Customer-favourable and requires no edit.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no specification-based exclusion appears in the rendered text; absence is Customer-favourable and requires no edit.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered Article 11 or Section 7.4 text; the redaction is confined to the indemnity trigger lists and time periods, not to a remedies sentence.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy is present in any rendered provision.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No cap is applied to Harpoon's indemnity; Section 11.5 limits only consequential damages. This is Customer-favourable (uncapped indemnity), so no cap should be inserted, but the element as written is not present.

elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element, but noted: Section 11.2 defence duty is present and supports the fallback IP structure if the redacted triggers include IP.

reasons: No operative redline was proposed, so there is nothing to test for minimality or intent damage; the analysis is a hold-for-review, which is the correct posture where the determinative text is redacted.

The preferred level is incomplete only because the substantive triggers of Sections 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted as "[***]". Four Harpoon-side triggers (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and the scope of AbbVie's own indemnity in 11.1 are unverifiable, so they are cannot_tell, not met.

The structural preferred elements are genuinely satisfied on the face of the text: express defence duty to AbbVie and Affiliates (11.2), notice (11.3), allocation of defence control (11.4.1), and reasonable cooperation (11.4.4). No edit is warranted to those.

The fallback level fails independently on operative language: there is no procure/modify/replace remedy and no refund-of-fees fallback remedy anywhere in the rendered text. If the unredacted 11.2 does not contain them, insert them as part of the IP-indemnity paragraph.

Do not insert the 3x-annual-fees super-cap. Harpoon's indemnity is presently uncapped (11.5 restricts only consequential damages), which is better than the fallback; adding the cap would be a self-inflicted concession and would fail the do-not-flag-favourable-language rule.

Section 7.4's cross-reference ("Subject to Section 11.2" for Third Party patent-infringement claims against AbbVie) is inference only and cannot substitute for an operative IP trigger; do not treat it as satisfying the IP element.

Action for the drafter: obtain the unredacted Sections 11.1 and 11.2. If 11.2 omits any of (a) IP infringement by the licensed compound/deliverables, (b) Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, (c) Harpoon-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of AbbVie data, or (d) Harpoon's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, add the missing sub-clauses into the existing 11.2 list rather than inserting a free-standing paragraph, to avoid duplicating the retained architecture. If 11.1 reaches beyond AbbVie-provided content and AbbVie's breach of law, narrow it in place.

Flagging as needs_review rather than proposing blind language is appropriate here: drafting an insertion against a redacted list risks duplicate or contradictory triggers, which would itself fail minimality.
